doubling than the cell achieves, never a slower one. The gate asked only for a factor

THIS IS THE ONE THAT BEARS ON THE ANSWER. The gap between route M and route P is
53% of a cell's protein, and at AUC 0.79 that missing mass is disproportionately
the UNSTUDIED proteome. Route P is immune to it -- grams of protein per cell do not
care what has been published -- which is the reason it is central and route H, which
is built out of a second detection-limited proteomics dataset, is not.

THE HONEST LIMIT
This predicts the doubling time a protein budget PERMITS, not the one a cell chooses.
A cell can always grow more slowly than its ribosomes allow, so the calculation is a
LOWER bound on T -- and the run says it is a lower bound that is NOT tight: 13.3 h
permitted against 24 h achieved. That is the result. It would be equally consistent
with the data if the real constraint were nucleotides, membrane, or a checkpoint, and
nothing here shows translation binds. What it shows is that translation does NOT bind,
to within the factor of 2.1 by which the four routes to A disagree. That spread,
not the gene-level noise (bootstrap +/- 2.16 h), is the whole uncertainty of this loop.
Two assumptions carry it and neither is tested here: that the 53% of proteome mass with no
measured half-life turns over at the same mass-weighted rate as the 47% that does,
and that Schwanhausser's NIH3T3 turnover transfers to a 24 h reference cell that is not NIH3T3.
